sections.h2: Who sends a Hendersonville property tax bill
sections.html:
A house inside Hendersonville is taxed twice, by Sumner County and by the City of Hendersonville, and the two bills come from different offices. The Sumner County Trustee collects the county share, and the city's finance office collects the city share. The Sumner County Assessor of Property sets the value both bills use.

Hendersonville is the largest city in Sumner County, on Old Hickory Lake about 18 miles northeast of Nashville. City hall is at 101 Maple Drive N, Hendersonville, TN 37075. The Trustee's office is in Gallatin at 355 North Belvedere Drive, Room 107, phone (615) 452-1260, open weekdays from eight to four-thirty. The Assessor can be reached at (615) 452-2412.

The city's Tax Structure page lists a Hendersonville rate of $0.5883 per $100 of assessed value and a Sumner County rate of $1.4210 per $100. Together that is $2.0093 per $100 of assessed value. Residential and farm property is assessed at 25% of appraised value, commercial and industrial at 40%, and personal property equipment at 30%.

The Board of Mayor and Aldermen approves the city budget each year in a process of about three months, with two readings and a public hearing before it takes effect. That hearing is where a change in the city rate would surface. Rates can change when the city and county pass new budgets, so ask the finance office and the Trustee for the figures on your own bill.

sections.h2: Due dates and how to pay
sections.html:
City taxes can be paid from the first Monday in October and are due by the last day of February. Interest of 1.5% a month starts March 1. The county bill follows the same February deadline, and Sumner County adds interest from March 1 as well.

Ways to pay a Hendersonville or Sumner County tax bill
BillPayment methodDetails
CityMailCheck payable to the City of Hendersonville, sent to 101 Maple Drive N; postmark date counts
CityIn personCity Hall takes cash, check, money order or card; a dropbox on the front portico is open around the clock for checks and money orders
CityOnlineCity payment portal; cards add a 2.95% convenience fee and an e-check carries a $2.95 fee
CountyOnline, mail, phone or in persontnpayments.com, top of the notice by mail, by phone, Room 107, or local banks listed on the back of the notice; cards cost 2.65% plus $1

The Trustee takes up to five partial payments by check or cash. Any unpaid portion starts collecting interest on March 1.

Contact the Sumner County Assessor at (615) 452-2412 for an informal review, then use the Sumner County Board of Equalization, then the State Board of Equalization. Informal reviews run in May and the county board convenes June 1 each year. Book your county board appointment well before the deadline, and call the assessor's office to learn the exact date for the current cycle. Sumner's last countywide reappraisal notices went out in 2024.

The assessor lists the kinds of evidence it accepts for homes:

  • Sales of comparable properties.
  • Recent photographs.
  • Insurance replacement value or a recent appraisal.
  • Costs to build, and the cost to cure any physical or functional problem.
  • Changes in the physical characteristics of the property.

Sumner County's Trustee runs the state relief program for elderly, disabled and disabled military service member homeowners, and also a tax freeze program for the county and part of the county's cities. Ask the Trustee whether the freeze covers your Hendersonville address, because the county describes it as covering only a portion of the cities.

Relief for people 65 and older and for disabled homeowners is income based. Relief for totally and permanently disabled military service members, and for their surviving spouses, is not. Applications are taken when the tax bills are mailed and must be finished no later than 35 days after the February payment deadline. Freeze applications open in September, and annual requalification is required. To book a phone or online appointment, call (615) 452-1260.

Relief is a payment toward the tax, not an exemption, so you still receive and must pay your bills. It applies to a primary residence only.

Both the city and the county bill stay with the parcel, so the closing agent should pull a payoff from each office. Sumner County shows verification of paid taxes under the online payment link, which helps confirm that a prior year is clear.

The Assessor's office handles mailing address changes for county bills, so call (615) 452-2412 after closing so notices reach the new owner. Questions about tax sales in Sumner County go to the Clerk and Master's office.

Deeds are recorded with the Sumner County Register of Deeds, which publishes its own records site. Under state rules the grantee, meaning the buyer, pays the transfer tax.

If you owe back tax, ask each office for a payoff figure before you set a closing date, and tell the title company early so it can pay both from your proceeds.

Hendersonville had 61,753 residents in the 2020 census and about 64,266 in the 2025 estimate, the tenth largest city in Tennessee. The city has 25,255 households, and owners occupy 71.7% of homes. The median owner-occupied value is $430,700, rent runs a median $1,653, and household income a median $97,200.

State Route 386 and U.S. 31E carry most traffic. A tornado struck the city on December 9, 2023, so ask for permit records on any house that had storm repairs. The city is governed by a mayor and twelve aldermen.

faqs.q: Does Hendersonville have its own property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The city levies $0.5883 per $100 of assessed value on top of the Sumner County rate of $1.4210. The city collects its own bill at 101 Maple Drive N, and the county Trustee collects the county bill in Gallatin.

faqs.q: When are Hendersonville property taxes due?
faqs.a: They are due by the last day of February. Payments open on the first Monday in October, and interest of 1.5% per month starts March 1. Mailed payments count on the postmark date.

faqs.q: How can I pay Hendersonville property tax online?
faqs.a: Use the online payment portal linked from the city's Tax Structure page. Cards carry a 2.95% convenience fee and e-checks a $2.95 processing fee, and both fees may change.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Hendersonville assessment?
faqs.a: Call the Sumner County Assessor at (615) 452-2412 for an informal review, which runs in May. The county Board of Equalization convenes June 1, and the State Board of Equalization is the next step.

faqs.q: Who do I call about senior tax relief in Hendersonville?
faqs.a: Call the Sumner County Trustee at (615) 452-1260. Applications are accepted when bills are mailed and until 35 days after the February deadline, and the office books appointments by phone or online.
